subject: mathematics
question_text: If tanθ = b/a, then prove that a cos2θ + b sin2θ = a.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Rewrite the condition
steps.margin_note: tanθ = b/a is a ratio of sine to cosine, so cross-multiplying gives a relation with no fraction in it — much easier to substitute.

recall.must_convey: That tanθ = b/a is rewritten as sinθ/cosθ = b/a and cross-multiplied to b cosθ = a sinθ.
accept: write tan as sin over cos and cross multiply to get b cos theta equals a sin theta
turn the condition into b cos theta equals a sin theta
tan theta ni sin by cos ga rasi cross multiply cheyyali
the condition becomes b cos theta equals a sin theta

steps.why: A condition with a fraction is awkward to substitute. Clearing it first is what makes the substitution below a single clean swap.
common_mistakes: Leaving the condition as a fraction.
Cross-multiplying the wrong way to a cosθ = b sinθ.
steps.memory_tip: Cross-multiply tanθ = b/a into b cosθ = a sinθ — a relation with no fraction, easy to substitute.

steps.label: Expand sin2θ and substitute
steps.margin_note: First mark. Expand sin2θ as 2 sinθ cosθ, then spot the b cosθ inside it and swap it for a sinθ using the condition.

recall.must_convey: That sin2θ is expanded to 2 sinθ cosθ, and that b cosθ inside it is replaced by a sinθ using the condition.
accept: expand sin two theta as two sin cos then replace b cos theta by a sin theta
use the double angle and then substitute the condition
the b cos theta becomes a sin theta so everything is in a
sin two theta expand chesi, b cos theta ni a sin theta ga marchali
substitute the condition inside the expansion

steps.why: The b has to disappear because the answer is just a. Grouping the expansion so that b cosθ appears as a unit is what lets the condition remove it.
common_mistakes: Expanding sin2θ but never grouping b with cosθ.
steps.memory_tip: Expand sin2θ = 2 sinθ cosθ, then spot the b cosθ inside and swap it for a sinθ.

steps.label: Expand cos2θ and cancel
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Choose cos2θ = 1 − 2sin²θ, not the other forms — it is the one whose second term cancels what is already there.

recall.must_convey: That cos2θ = 1 − 2sin²θ is used, and that the two sin²θ terms cancel to leave a.
accept: use cos two theta equals one minus two sin squared so the sine terms cancel leaving a
expand cos two theta and the two terms cancel
choose the form that cancels and the answer is a
cos two theta ni one minus two sin square ga rasthe cancel ayi a vasthundi
the sin squared terms cancel leaving just a

steps.why: cos2θ has three standard forms and only one of them cancels here. Choosing the right one is the whole skill of the last line.
common_mistakes: Using cos2θ = 2cos²θ − 1 and being left with a mixture.
steps.memory_tip: Choose cos2θ = 1 − 2sin²θ — the one form whose second term cancels what is already there.

insider_note: Turn tanθ = b/a into b cosθ = a sinθ and substitute it into the sin2θ term — that substitution is the key step. Then cos2θ = 1 − 2sin²θ makes the remaining terms cancel.
